I understand! When you press `Ctrl+C`, the process terminates/exits completely — there's no pause/resume capability with a standard shell process.

## The Problem:

```bash
# This stops the process and kills it:
Ctrl+C  → process exits, you can't resume

# What you want:
Ctrl+SPACE → pause current task (like hitting "pause" in an app)
Resume later → and continue from where you left off
```

## Solutions:

### Option 1: **Run in background (tmux/screen)**
```bash
# Start in tmux with auto-suspend
tmux new-session -d -n python_agent

# This creates a process in a separate session you can detach from

# Detach from tmux (Ctrl+B, D) — process keeps running in background
# Attach back to resume: tmux attach -t python_agent
```

### Option 2: **Use a wrapper script with pause**
```bash
# Create a script that tracks state and can be paused
cat > /tmp/agent_wrapper.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
STATE_FILE=/tmp/agent_state.json
RUNNING=true

while $RUNNING; do
    # Your agent loop here
    if [[ $RUNNING != true ]]; then
        echo "$STATE_RUNNER_PID:$RUNNING" > "$STATE_FILE"
        break
    fi
done
EOF

chmod +x /tmp/agent_wrapper.sh
```

### Option 3: **Use Python signal handlers**
If I code myself, I can create a pauseable agent:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import signal

PAUSED = False

signal.signal(signal.SIGUSR1, lambda s, f: setattr(signal, '_paused', True))
signal.signal(signal.SIGUSR2, lambda s, f: setattr(signal, '_paused', False))

while True:
    if not getattr(signal, '_paused', False):
        # Do work

```

)

check_download() {
    local model="$1"
    local desc="$2"
    
    echo "=== ${desc} ==="
    
    # Check file exists
    if [[ -f "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${model}" ]]; then
        echo "✅ Already downloaded: ${model}"
        ls -lh "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${model}" 2>/dev/null || echo "   File not found"
        return
    fi
    
    echo "⚠️  Not found, trying direct download..."
    
    # Try various direct download URLs (no HF token)
    for url in
        "https://huggingface.co/jartine/${model%/resolve/main/${model}"
        "https://huggingface.co/microsoft/${model%/resolve/main/${model}"
        "https://huggingface.co/microsoft/LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instructions/resolve/main/LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct-q4_K_M.gguf"
        "https://huggingface.co/microsoft/LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/main/llama-3.2-1b-instruct-q4_K_M.gguf"

        "https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.3-GGUF/resolve/main/mistral-7b-v0.3-q4_K_M.gguf"

        echo "   → ${url}"

            echo "   ✅ Success!"
            ls -lh "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${model}"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    
    echo "   ⚠️  Not available directly (may need HF token)" >&2
    echo "   🌐 Try: ${url}" >&2
    return 1
}

check_and_download_model() {
    check_download "$1" "$2"
}

# Main loop
if [[ -z "${HF_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
    echo "No HF_TOKEN available, using direct download URLs"
else
    echo "HF_TOKEN present, checking huggingface.co..."
fi

# Get first model that's available
for model in "${MODELS[@]}"; do
    desc=$(echo "$model" | sed 's/.*-//' | xargs)
    check_download "${model}" "$desc" || true
done

# Summary
echo ""
echo "=== Summary ==="
echo "Models directory: ${OUTPUT_DIR}"
find "${OUTPUT_DIR}" -name "*.gguf" -exec ls -lh {} \; 2>/dev/null || true

# List all available models

echo "✅ Ready to use with Ollama:"
echo "   ollama serve --model ${OUTPUT_DIR}/gguf/*.gguf"
echo "   ollama create mymodel -f ${OUTPUT_DIR}/gguf/*.gguf"

# project scope

This project allows the running of local agents as supporters. Those agents will be used for supporting the development of FEM/blender integration, energy optimization engines and CV/ML on embedded devices.

- goal :: a local coding assistant
- stack :: IDE: emacs, LLM serve: ollama, OS: ubuntu 26
- workflow :: within emacs, code will be executed via python REPL and .org code blocks
- purpose :: data analytics, no need for production code, simple and readable code, avoid abstraction
- test :: no successful results without testing and documenting
- language :: the project language is English, don't translate
- config :: python programs uses json files as config, run logs will be added to that json and saved into a `runs/` folder for versioning

# project structure

Project structure :

- assistants :: coding assistants
  - [[./agent_call.org][agent_call.org]] :: detailed agent instructions to run this project and to explain it's outpt
  - [[./aider/][aider/]] :: conf files to use with aider
  - [[./config.json][config.json]] :: the pi-coding-agent config file
  - [[./emacs][emacs]] :: conf files for agentic usage of emacs in org mode
- deployment ::
  - [[./ansible/][ansible/]] :: ansible script for remote deployment (i.e. jetson)
  - [[./docker-compose.yml][docker-compose.yml]] :: to start mcp_server and mcp_client
  - [[./logs/][logs/]] :: application outputs for debugging
  - [[./nginx/][nginx/]] :: web server configuration to deploy this project (i.e. on jetson)
  - [[./ollama/][ollama/]] :: ollama container and conf
  - [[./mcphub/][mcphub/]] :: to monitor mcp applications
  - [[./morpheus/][morpheus/]] :: nvidia onnx cybersecurity ML enrichment on cuda
  - [[./test/][test/]] :: collection of script to test the configurations
- apps ::
  - [[./blender_mcp/][blender_mcp]] :: definition of the mcp addon to integrate with blender
  - [[./mcp-client/][mcp-client]] :: app to interact with the mcp-server
  - [[./mcp-server/][mcp-server/]] :: app exposing the mcp tools for the language models mainly consumed by gptel
- context ::
  - [[./doc/][doc/]] :: machine generated documentation of useful components
- presentation ::
  - [[./html/][html]] :: slides and diagrams to present the project
  - [[./icon][icon/]] :: useful icons for the presentation
  - [[./img/][img/]] :: images for the documentation
  - [[./html/js/][js/]] :: javascript for the presentation
  - [[./html/css/][css/]] :: style sheets for professional technical documentation
  - [[./data/][data/]] :: input data like json graphs
  - [[./script/][script/]] :: collection of script to run this project

# agent

- local  :: you are developing local applications for pilot test, no need to over engineer the project
- docker :: the applications run locally or in docker, no need for virtual env

# project outcome

- this project provides agentic support to data scientists. The LLMs run locally with ollama, both on ubuntu with Nvidia GPU
- the data scientists need to build an MCP server to allow their programming to interact with different systems:
  - [[./blender-mcp/][blender-mcp/]] :: blender for 3d modeling

  - [[../phys_opt/][phys_opt]] :: optimization engine for graphs
  - [[../pose_estimate_py/][pose_estimate_py]] :: computer vision (pose estimate)
  - knowledge graphs

- Audience :: scientific/technical blog

- JS :: minimal usage, ideally none
- images :: centered with a opaque background and some shadow
- headers :: h1, h2,h3... should have similar shades but different and elegant
- navbar :: minimal, few links, elegant, discrete

- footer :: put intertino as owner and license [[https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/][CC by-nc-sa]] 

# tech stack

The main libraries:

- python: ollama, mcp
- js: d3.js
- web: html/css

# hardware

The project is optimized to run locally on:

   - CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 with NPU

   - RAM: 32GB 
2. [[https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin/nano-super-developer-kit/][Nvidia Jetson orin nano]]:
   - 2x ARM Cortex-A55 cores
